Official DHS indicator estimates for Bangladesh

Source: R/data.R
bdhs_indicators.Rd

Every indicator value the DHS Program publishes for the nine Bangladesh DHS rounds (1993-94 to 2022), nationally and by region and background characteristics, as released through the DHS Program Indicator Data API. These are the official estimates of the survey final reports and STATcompiler; use them directly or to validate your own estimates.

Usage

bdhs_indicators

Format

A tibble with 310,528 rows and 25 columns:

survey_id

DHS survey identifier, e.g. "BD2022DHS".

survey_year

Survey year.

survey_label

Year label, e.g. "2017-18".

indicator_id

DHS indicator id, e.g. "FE_FRTR_W_TFR" (total fertility rate). A few ids are reused for two indicators; the pair (indicator_id, indicator_order) is unique (see bdhs_indicator_catalog).

indicator_order

DHS sort order of the indicator; together with indicator_id it identifies the indicator.

indicator

Indicator label.

indicator_type

Type of value: "I" indicator, "D" weighted denominator, "U" unweighted denominator, "T" distribution total (100 percent), "S" special answers (don't know/missing), "E" sampling error, "C" confidence interval, "N" number of cases (e.g. women interviewed).

breakdown

"national" (the total, is_total), "subnational" (by region) or "background" (any other characteristic). The DHS API also returns subnational rows for breakdown=background.

characteristic_id

DHS characteristic id (1000 = total).

characteristic_category

Characteristic category, e.g. "Residence", "Region", "Wealth quintile", "Total".

characteristic_label

Characteristic, e.g. "Urban". Region labels use the current spellings; labels starting with ".." are subregions of the region above (e.g. "..Rangpur" within "Rajshahi/Rangpur"), so trend-consistent aggregates and the regions as surveyed are both present.

characteristic_order

DHS sort order of the characteristic.

by_variable_id

Id of a further disaggregation (0 = none).

by_variable_label

Label of the further disaggregation, e.g. a reference period such as "Five years preceding the survey", or an age group; NA if none.

region_id

DHS API region id for regional rows (e.g. "BDDHS2022360004"); joins to reg_id in bdhs_regions and in bdhs_boundaries(). NA for other rows.

level_rank

Administrative level of a regional row (1 = the regions as surveyed; NA for trend aggregates and non-regional rows).

value

The estimate, in the units of the indicator (percent, rate per 1,000, mean, number, ...).

precision

Number of decimals with which the DHS Program presents the value.

denom_weighted, denom_unweighted

Weighted and unweighted denominators (number of cases), where published.

ci_low, ci_high

Lower and upper bounds of the 95 percent confidence interval; published only for a few indicators (e.g. maternal mortality).

is_total

TRUE for the national total.

is_preferred

TRUE for the DHS Program's preferred (headline) value when an indicator is published several ways (e.g. for several reference periods).

default_view

TRUE for the preferred row of a survey x indicator x characteristic cell, or for every row of a cell that has no preferred row (e.g. mortality by wealth, published only for the 10-year period).

Source

The DHS Program Indicator Data API, data endpoint (breakdown=all), https://api.dhsprogram.com, API version 8.1, retrieved 2026-10-26: "The DHS Program Indicator Data API, The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) Program. ICF. Originally funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). Available from api.dhsprogram.com. [Accessed 2026-10-26]". Built by data-raw/01-fetch-dhs-api.R and data-raw/02-build-api-datasets.R.

Details

One row is one value: survey x indicator x characteristic (e.g. "Urban", "Rajshahi", "Highest wealth quintile") x by-variable (e.g. reference period). Where an indicator is published several ways, is_preferred flags the headline value; default_view keeps exactly what a user should see by default.

The API returned 321,440 rows on 2026-10-26, of which 10,912 were exact duplicates (every 2022 region row twice, an artefact of the API's geometry table); they have been removed. Non-preferred rows are kept.

See also

bdhs_indicator_catalog for definitions, bdhs_official() to query these values, bdhs_estimate() and bdhs_validate() to reproduce them from microdata.

Examples

# Total fertility rate, national, every round
tfr <- bdhs_indicators[bdhs_indicators$indicator_id == "FE_FRTR_W_TFR" &
  bdhs_indicators$is_total & bdhs_indicators$is_preferred, ]
tfr[, c("survey_label", "value")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 2
#>   survey_label value
#>   <chr>        <dbl>
#> 1 1993-94        3.4
#> 2 1996-97        3.3
#> 3 1999-00        3.3
#> 4 2004           3  
#> 5 2007           2.7
#> 6 2011           2.3
#> 7 2014           2.3
#> 8 2017-18        2.3
#> 9 2022           2.3

# Under-5 mortality by division, 2022 (regions as surveyed)
u5 <- bdhs_indicators[bdhs_indicators$indicator_id == "CM_ECMR_C_U5M" &
  bdhs_indicators$survey_id == "BD2022DHS" &
  bdhs_indicators$breakdown == "subnational" &
  bdhs_indicators$level_rank %in% 1 & bdhs_indicators$default_view, ]
u5[, c("characteristic_label", "by_variable_label", "value")]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   characteristic_label by_variable_label              value
#>   <chr>                <chr>                          <dbl>
#> 1 Barishal             Ten years preceding the survey    43
#> 2 ..Chattogram         Ten years preceding the survey    36
#> 3 ..Sylhet             Ten years preceding the survey    61
#> 4 ..Dhaka              Ten years preceding the survey    36
#> 5 ..Mymensingh         Ten years preceding the survey    44
#> 6 Khulna               Ten years preceding the survey    31
#> 7 ..Rangpur            Ten years preceding the survey    46
#> 8 ..Rajshahi           Ten years preceding the survey    27
